# Final Experiment Design — TorchOpt explicit gradient differentiation vs standard PyTorch autograd

Design-only specification. No experiment is executed in this environment. No results, no pseudo-outputs, no projected plots are claimed.

## Binding decisions applied verbatim

- D1 scope: T1 (ridge regression, convex) and T2 (2-layer MLP, non-convex). T3 (CNN) is dropped and re-enters the design only if, during writing or pre-execution review, the stability axis is demonstrated to be underdetermined. As of this draft the stability axis is supported by T1 and T2 alone, so T3 remains absent.
- D2 API surface: candidate TorchOpt names retained as references; every TorchOpt invocation in pseudo-example code is tagged "[verify]"; the design contains a Source-verification gate placed before section (iii); if the verified names and signatures do not match the documented surface, the design is rewritten, not relabelled.
- D3 environment: float64 throughout; CPU only with an explicit acknowledgment that torch.cuda.Event is unavailable and that CUDA-side TorchOpt optimisations such as kernel fusion and graph caching are not measured on this host; OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 plus MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 plus torch.set_num_threads(1) as primary; a single set_num_threads(4) sensitivity repeat; taskset -c 0-3 for CPU affinity; software-version manifest is a required artifact; no float32 runs.
- D4 fairness for create_graph=True: standard, documented form with no allow_unused, no torch.compile, no manual activation checkpointing. The best-practices variant (create_graph=True plus torch.compile) is recorded only in section (x) as a future GPU-host path.
- D5 metric hierarchy: both computation time and numerical stability are primary in general. On this CPU-only host, stability plus algorithmic-flop accounting is the primary evidentiary axis, time is secondary, and the preamble explicitly states that CUDA-leaning TorchOpt optimisations are out of scope on CPU. This is an honest environmental ceiling, not a design bug.
- D6 reuse-claim isolation: the primary ablation table preserves the three-way separation of effects — Treatment A (implicit-diff hypergradient with reuse) versus Treatment B (MetaOptimizer-style inner-state reuse without implicit-diff) versus C2 (unrolled create_graph=True without reuse). The design collapses to two independent comparisons (A versus C2 and B versus C2) only if the Source-verification gate finds that TorchOpt does not expose two distinct differentiable paths.

---

## (i) Research question and pre-registered hypotheses

Research question. Will TorchOpt's explicit gradient-differentiation API — characterised by reuse of intermediate data and minimisation of memory allocation — reduce computation time and improve numerical stability relative to standard PyTorch autograd implementations?

Pre-registered hypotheses. Direction and magnitude are stated as a priori expectations only; they are not numerical guarantees. The design creates the conditions under which these hypotheses can be evaluated; it does not pre-commit to a result.

H1 (computation time, secondary on this CPU host per D5). On T2 with K at least 100, the wall-clock per inner solve under TorchOpt's explicit differentiable optimisation pathway (Treatments A and B) is lower than under unrolled create_graph=True autograd (C2). Expected direction: lower under Treatment. Expected magnitude: sub-linear or flat growth with K for Treatment A, near-linear growth with K for C2, but no specific factor is asserted. On T1 the magnitude is expected to be small because the inner problem is linear and the autograd baselines are already cheap.

H2 (numerical stability, primary on this CPU host per D5). On T1 with K at least 100, the relative-error stability proxy of Treatment A is closer to the analytical reference than that of C2. On T2 (no analytical reference), the same proxy is evaluated against C4 at a tight tolerance or against central finite differences in float64. Expected direction: lower rel_err for Treatment. Expected magnitude: not pre-specified.

Secondary hypotheses (also expectations, not guarantees):

H3 (state-reuse isolation). Treatment B is expected to show an intermediate speed versus C2 advantage at large K, smaller than A versus C2 in magnitude, because reuse alone without implicit-diff saves memory accesses but not the unroll computation.

H4 (gradient norm scaling). The condition number of the implicit-system matrix kappa(A) is expected to grow sub-linearly with K for the implicit-diff paths, while the unrolled gradient norm blows up linearly in K under ill-conditioned choices of inner step size.

---

## (ii) Rationale

Why these tasks. T1 (synthetic Gaussian-design ridge regression with scalar outer variable lambda) gives a closed-form hypergradient: g_ref(lambda) equals the derivative of L_outer along the closed-form solution path w*(lambda). This is the cleanest possible test of the numerical-stability claim because the answer is known exactly. T2 (2-layer MLP with cross-entropy on synthetic classification, scalar outer variable alpha) exercises non-convex conditioning where unrolled differentiation methods compound round-off as K grows; this is the regime in which the reuse-of-intermediates claim is most load-bearing. Together (T1 times T2) gives the minimum factorisation that spans both convex and non-convex inner losses. The K-sweep {10, 100, 1000} spans one decade below and one above the canonical MAML inner-loop length and provides the primary speed-and-stability axis.

Why these controls. C2 (autograd with create_graph=True in documented standard form) is the most informative fair-naive comparator for an unrolled inner loop with the optimiser-state view of TorchOpt. C1 (vanilla loss.backward(), no graph retention) is the practitioner default and the cheap reference. C3 (torch.func or functorch.jacrev) is the modern JAX-style alternative and the most likely competitor on speed. C4 (hand-rolled implicit-diff solving the system (I minus d-step/d-w) v equals g via CG at a fixed tight tolerance) is explicitly labelled a stability reference, not a baseline.

Why these two primary metrics. Wall-clock per inner solve in milliseconds is the direct measurement of the time claim. The stability proxy rel_err comparing the method's hypergradient to a high-precision reference (analytical for T1, finite-difference or C4 at tight tolerance for T2) is the direct measurement of the stability claim. The implicit-system matrix condition number kappa(A) and residual norm(A v minus g) at termination are secondary stability signals that apply only to implicit-diff paths. Outer-loss variance across the R seeds is a coarse but robust secondary stability indicator.

Why the held-constant environment. Pinning threads, BLAS, and seeds makes timing differences attributable to algorithmic choice rather than scheduler contention. Restricting to float64 isolates numerical-stability signals from float32 round-off — the only honest precision regime in which to evaluate the stability claim. Scalar outer hyperparameters are an explicit scope choice so that the analytical reference for T1 and the central-difference reference for T2 remain tractable.

---

## (ix) Source-verification gate (placed before (iii) per binding)

This gate executes before any later section is treated as executable. It produces a go-or-rewrite decision.

Local environment status, recorded factually.

TorchOpt is not present in this workspace. The directory /workspace contains only task.json. A filesystem-wide search for any directory or file matching the pattern *torchopt* on this bubblewrap host returns zero results. The Python interpreter is 3.12.3; the statements import torch and import torchopt both raise ModuleNotFoundError. The runtime is bubblewrap and the network is disabled. Consequently, no local verification of TorchOpt API names, function signatures, default arguments, default solver tolerances, default iteration caps, or runtime behaviour is possible from inside this environment. The candidate surface torchopt.diff.implicit.grad, torchopt.MetaOptimizer, and torchopt.diff.functional is drawn from public TorchOpt documentation at large and is not confirmed against an installed source. Every TorchOpt call in pseudo-example code is therefore tagged "[verify]" — a marker that indicates the documentation intent only and that replacement is required if a source confirmation disagrees.

Verification procedure when execution becomes feasible. (1) Acquire a TorchOpt source checkout matching the target Python and PyTorch versions; record the commit SHA in the manifest from section (iv). (2) For every "[verify]" invocation site, locate the corresponding function or method in the source. (3) Verify that the module path, the function name, the function signature, the default solver tolerance, the default iteration cap, and the inner-state reuse semantics match the description in section (iii). (4) Record the verified name, signature, and default tolerance in an appendix of the experiment report. (5) If any verification step fails, the design is rewritten to use the actual surface — names are not relabelled to preserve the appearance of having used the intended API. In particular, if TorchOpt exposes only one of the two intended differentiable paths so that the implicit-diff reuse and the MetaOptimizer-state reuse cannot be separated, the design simplifies per binding D6 to two independent comparisons (A versus C2 and B versus C2) instead of fabricating a separation.

The Source-verification gate occupies one working day in the feasibility estimate of section (vii). No later section of this design is implemented before the gate passes.

---

## (iii) Treatments and controls

Single table covering all six methods. The labels "[verify]" mark every TorchOpt call as documented-intention only until the Source-verification gate confirms them.

| ID  | Method                                                                              | Brief description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Role                                     | Reuse axis                                |
|-----|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| A   | TorchOpt implicit-gradient path — torchopt.diff.implicit.grad [verify]              | Wraps the inner loss and the outer variable; returns a hypergradient computed via an implicit-differentiation fixed-point or linear solve; inner intermediates are reused rather than unrolled K times.                                                                                                                                          | Treatment — implicit-diff reuse          | Full (intermediates plus hypergrad reuse) |
| B   | TorchOpt MetaOptimizer path — torchopt.MetaOptimizer, MetaSGD, MetaAdam [verify]    | MetaOptimizer (or MetaSGD or MetaAdam subclass [verify]) wraps a persistent inner optimiser whose state — for example momentum or Adam second-moment — survives across the K inner steps; outer hypergradient via torch.autograd.grad on the meta-update.                                                                                       | Treatment — inner-state reuse            | Inner optimiser state reuse only          |
| C1  | Vanilla torch.autograd — no create_graph                                            | loss.backward() is called K times separately with no graph retention; the hypergradient is derived from the final inner state by hand.                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Baseline — practitioner default         | None                                      |
| C2  | autograd with create_graph=True — documented standard form                         | loss.backward(create_graph=True) is called K times; outer hypergradient via torch.autograd.grad. Documented standard form: no allow_unused, no torch.compile, no manual activation checkpointing.                                                                                                                                            | Baseline — fair naive unrolled comparator | None                                      |
| C3  | torch.func / functorch.jacrev                                                       | Modern JAX-style reverse-mode AD applied to the inner-loop functional form.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Baseline — modern alternative            | Library-dependent                          |
| C4  | Hand-rolled implicit-diff reference — solves (I minus d-step/d-w) v equals g via CG | Direct solution of the inner-loop implicit equation by conjugate gradient at a fixed tight tolerance. Labelled a numerical-stability reference, not a speed baseline.                                                                                                                                                                          | Reference — stability ceiling             | None (direct solve)                       |

Primary ablation (per binding D6). The three-way table A versus B versus C2 is the headline ablation and tests two effects in isolation: A versus C2 isolates the implicit-diff reuse claim; B versus C2 isolates the inner-state reuse claim; C1 and C3 are secondary contextual comparators; C4 is a stability reference. If the Source-verification gate finds that TorchOpt exposes only one differentiable path so that A and B cannot be separated, the ablation collapses to two independent pairwise comparisons (A versus C2) and (B versus C2) without other design changes.

Pseudocode flavour — TorchOpt calls tagged "[verify]":

```
# T1 (ridge, scalar outer lambda), method-header sketch
def make_method(name, inner_lr, K, lambda_init):
    if name == "A":
        # [verify] module path, function name, default solver tolerance, default iteration cap
        def hypergrad(w0, X, y, lam):
            loss_inner = lambda w: ((X @ w - y) ** 2).mean() + lam * (w ** 2).mean()
            return torchopt.diff.implicit.grad(loss_inner, lam, wrt=lam, argnums=(0,))(w0)[0]  # [verify]
        return hypergrad
    elif name == "B":
        # [verify] MetaOptimizer and MetaSGD surface area only — confirmation against source required
        inner = torchopt.MetaSGD(net, inner_lr)            # [verify]
        meta_opt = torchopt.MetaOptimizer(inner, warp=True) # [verify]
        ...
    elif name == "C2":
        def hypergrad(w0, X, y, lam):
            w = w0.detach().requires_grad_(True)
            for _ in range(K):
                loss = ((X @ w - X @ y) ** 2).mean() + lam * (w ** 2).mean()
                grad = torch.autograd.grad(loss, w, create_graph=True)[0]   # standard documented form
                w = (w - inner_lr * grad).detach().requires_grad_(True)
            # final-state hypergradient by-hand from the terminal w
            ...
        return hypergrad
    # ... C1, C3, C4 follow the same per-method-header pattern
```

---

## (iv) Held-constant environment (separate section)

Everything in this section is held constant across cells; it is intentionally not mixed with the method descriptions in (iii).

dtype. float64 throughout. No float32 runs anywhere in the design. Torch default-dtype is set to float64 at run start.

device. CPU only. The host Runtime is bubblewrap with gpu_enabled equal to false (per environment note in task.json). torch.cuda.Event is unavailable in this environment. This is an explicit environmental ceiling: the time axis here does not measure CUDA-leaning TorchOpt optimisations (kernel fusion, autograd-graph caching, compiled-graph reuse). The stability axis is independent of GPU availability and remains the primary evidentiary axis on this host.

thread pinning (primary run). OMP_NUM_THREADS equals 1; MKL_NUM_THREADS equals 1; torch.set_num_threads(1) at run start.

thread sensitivity (single-axis probe only). The main run is repeated once with torch.set_num_threads(4) to sample one point of thread-sensitivity. This is the only thread-sensitivity exploration in the design — no other thread counts.

CPU affinity. taskset -c 0-3 is applied to all worker processes to suppress scheduler noise on the 24-logical-CPU host.

BLAS. The BLAS implementation that ships with the PyTorch CPU build — OpenBLAS or MKL, whichever is present — is recorded once in the manifest and is not swapped mid-experiment. The version of the BLAS in use is logged.

Software manifest (required artifact). Exact versions of Python, torch, torchopt, numpy, scipy. TorchOpt source git rev-parse HEAD recorded by the Source-verification gate (D2). Linux kernel version. Environment variables logged at run start. taskset invocation logged at run start.

Seeds. One master seed. For replicate r in {1 .. R} the per-replicate seed is seed_r = master_seed XOR r; the same seed_r is used identically across all methods within that replicate, enabling the paired statistics in (vi).

Inner-optimizer hyperparameters. Held constant within each task across methods.

Inner step K. Held constant per cell across methods.

Outer (hyper) optimizer. Plain SGD with a fixed step size, identical across methods, so that any time difference is attributable to inner-loop differentiation rather than outer-loop internal cost.

Outer hyperparameter dimensionality. Scalar. For T1 the outer hyperparameter is lambda (scalar regularizer strength). For T2 the outer hyperparameter is alpha (scalar inner learning rate). Vector-valued outer hyperparameters are out of scope; they would change the implicit-diff linear-system conditioning profile and are listed as an open question in (x).

Inner loss reduction. Mean. This choice affects hypergradient magnitude; it is fixed across methods so that stability comparisons are not aliased to a reduction choice.

Implicit-diff solver tolerance and iteration cap. Identical default tolerance and identical default iteration cap across Treatments A and the A-vs-B equivalents, identical defaults across C4 at the tight-tolerance reference level. A tolerance sweep at {1e-3, 1e-6, 1e-9} is a separate feasibility sub-experiment described in (vii); drops first under budget pressure.

Dataset. Synthetic, generated once per (task, K, seed_r) cell and reused across methods within that cell.

---

## (v) Measurement protocol

Execution proceeds per cell, where a cell is the tuple (task, method, K).

Step 1 — gate. Confirm the Source-verification gate (ix) has passed. If the gate has not passed, do not run any cell.

Step 2 — environment. Export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, MKL_NUM_THREADS=1; call torch.set_num_threads(1); run under taskset -c 0-3; call torch.set_default_dtype(torch.float64); record the manifest fields.

Step 3 — data and initialisation. Generate the synthetic dataset D_r for the (task, K, seed_r) tuple. Initialise inner and outer parameters as deterministic functions of seed_r; the same functions are used for every method in the replicate, so initial-state seed is paired across methods.

Step 4 — warm-up. Five full inner-solve roundtrips are run without timing. Purpose: amortise first-time allocations and BLAS dispatch.

Step 5 — timed run. R at-least-30 rounds. For each round r in {1 .. R}:

  a. Reset the torch and numpy random states from seed_r.
  b. t0 = time.perf_counter_ns().
  c. Execute K inner-optimizer steps under the cell's chosen differentiation mode.
  d. Compute the hypergradient with respect to the outer variable.
  e. Apply one outer SGD update step at the fixed outer step size.
  f. t1 = time.perf_counter_ns(); record dt = (t1 - t0) / 1e6 milliseconds.

Step 6 — per-round metadata. In addition to dt_r, record g_method_r (the hypergradient vector), L_inner_terminal_r (inner loss at step K), and — for implicit-diff methods only (Treatments A and reference C4) — the apparent residual norm(A v minus g) at termination and the condition number kappa(A) of the implicit-system matrix (if the solver does not expose kappa(A), it is computed post-hoc with numpy.linalg.cond on the assembled A).

Step 7 — proxies. Capture tracemalloc peak around one full inner solve per cell. Labelled explicitly as proxy in the results, not primary evidence, because CPU tracemalloc is a Python-level allocator trace and not a tensor-level memory profile.

Step 8 — per-cell outputs. Write one per-cell artifact bundle for (task, K, method, seed_master) containing: dt_r (length R), g_method_r series, g_ref series (computed per replicate), impl_residual_* series for implicit-diff cells, cond_* series for implicit-diff cells, L_inner_terminal_r series, tracemalloc peak.

Stability proxy for T1 — convex ridge, analytical reference. For ridge regression with normal-equation inner solution w*(lambda) equal to (X^T X plus lambda I)^(-1) X^T y, the hypergradient g_ref(lambda) equals the derivative of L_outer along the closed-form path. The stability proxy is

    rel_err_T1(method, r) = || g_method_r minus g_ref(lambda) ||_2 / || g_ref(lambda) ||_2

with g_ref recomputed on the same D_r and the same lambda per replicate. For implicit-diff methods, additionally report

    impl_residual_T1(method, r) = || A(lambda_r) v_r minus g_r ||_2
    cond_T1(method, r) = kappa( A(lambda_r) )

Stability proxy for T2 — non-convex MLP, finite-difference or C4 reference. No analytical reference is available. Two references are admissible: (a) C4 at a tighter tolerance than the cell's default; (b) central finite differences in float64 at step h approximately 1e-5 on alpha. The reference-of-record for T2 is C4 at tight tolerance by default; central finite differences at h approximately 1e-5 is the operational fallback if C4 cannot be made tighter than the cell default. The stability proxy is

    rel_err_T2(method, r) = || g_method_r minus g_ref ||_2 / || g_ref ||_2

The finite-difference reference is paid once per replicate per task; the cell's round-level timing is applied only to the method's own inner solve, not to the reference. Richardson extrapolation is permissible as a sensitivity check but is not the primary reference.

Memory proxy. CPU tracemalloc peak around one inner solve per cell. Labelled proxy only, not primary evidence.

The exact TorchOpt API names used — for example, the function formerly or currently named torchopt.diff.implicit.grad [verify] for Treatment A, and the solver argument list [verify] — are not locked until the Source-verification gate (ix) has passed and the verified names are appended to the experiment report.

---

## (vi) Statistical analysis

Unit of analysis. One replicate r in {1 .. R}, paired across methods by seed_r (and hence by D_r and initial-state seed).

Primary statistic. Wilcoxon signed-rank test, paired by seed_r, applied to:

  - the timing vector dt_r(method=baseline) minus dt_r(method=Treatment) for each (Treatment, baseline) pair;
  - the stability vector rel_err_r(method=baseline) minus rel_err_r(method=Treatment), aligned in sign so that "lower is better" for the Treatment.

Multiple-comparison correction. Holm correction across the family of comparisons within a (task, K) cell. The number of pairwise comparisons per cell is |Treatments| times |Baselines| = 2 times 3 = 6 (Treatments A, B times Baselines C1, C2, C3); Holm controls family-wise error rate at alpha = 0.05 over this family. Bonferroni is recorded as a sensitivity check (more conservative); Holm is the headline correction.

Per-cell reporting. Per (task, K, method):

  - the median of dt_r and the IQR (p25, p75) of dt_r;
  - the p95 of dt_r as a tail-latency indicator;
  - the median of rel_err_r and the IQR (p25, p75) of rel_err_r;
  - the median and p95 of kappa(A) for implicit-diff cells;
  - the median and p95 of impl_residual for implicit-diff cells.

Per pairwise test within a cell:

  - the Wilcoxon W statistic, the Holm-adjusted p-value, and the median signed difference Delta-tilde, with a 95 percent bootstrap confidence interval (B = 2000 resamples, seed fixed).

Pre-registered effect-size threshold. A difference is classified as meaningful only when the Holm-adjusted p-value is below 0.05 AND the absolute ratio |Delta-tilde divided by max(p75-minus-p25 across the two methods, 1e-12)| is at least 0.5. Cells where the Holm-adjusted p-value is greater than or equal to 0.05 are reported as "no detectable difference" and are NOT reported as "no effect". Smaller-than-threshold effects are not claimed as wins or losses under this design. Paired Cohen's d and Cliff's delta are computed from the recorded per-cell data and recorded as sensitivity descriptors but are not the headline effect-size metric.

Power. With R = 30 paired replicates and alpha = 0.05 (two-sided), the Wilcoxon signed-rank test has approximately 80 percent power to detect effect sizes around 0.5 SD in the paired differences; this is the source of the |Delta-tilde/IQR| at-least-0.5 threshold above. Roughly 15-percent-level speed-ups are detectable in well-behaved cells; smaller speed-ups will be reported as "no detectable difference".

---

## (vii) Feasibility (one page)

Runtime environment required. Not available in the current host. A CUDA-capable host is required for the eventual execution.

- Python at version 3.10 or newer. The current host Python 3.12.3 satisfies this.
- pip install torch torchopt numpy scipy, with the GPU-CUDA build of torch matched to the host CUDA driver. The current host is bubblewrap with network disabled and no PyTorch nor TorchOpt preinstalled; it is not the right host for execution.
- Source checkout of TorchOpt (not only the wheel) for the Source-verification gate, with git rev-parse HEAD recorded in the manifest.

Per-cell wall-clock estimate (single pinned core, indicative, to be calibrated at execution).

  - T1, K = 10 — a few seconds per replicate per method; cell at R = 30 about a few minutes.
  - T1, K = 100 — tens of seconds per replicate per method; cell about tens of minutes.
  - T1, K = 1000 — order of one to a few minutes per replicate per method; cell about one to two hours; C2 dominates.
  - T2, K = 10 — tens of seconds per replicate per method; cell about tens of minutes.
  - T2, K = 100 — one to several minutes per replicate per method; cell about one to a few hours.
  - T2, K = 1000 — tens of minutes to hours per replicate; full cell many hours to a day. C2 dominates; Treatments are faster by hypothesis.

Drop order under compute budget pressure.

  1. First drop: tolerance sweep (solver tolerance at {1e-3, 1e-6, 1e-9} treated as a single sub-experiment; the main run repeats the default-tolerance cells only).
  2. Second drop: Adam sub-experiment at K = 100 (the SGD-with-momentum inner optimizer is the default and is retained).
  3. Third drop: thread-sensitivity repeat at set_num_threads(4) (only if the primary single-thread run times are well-behaved).

Minimal scope (priority-1, budget-constrained path). T1 plus T2 with K fixed to 100 and 1000 (drop K = 10), all six methods, R = 30, no thread-sensitivity sweep, no tolerance sweep. Tests H1 and H2 along the conjunctive stability-time axis at K >= 100 with the most informative K-sweep length halved. Indicative wall-clock: low single-digit CPU-hours.

Ambitious scope (full design as specified). T1 plus T2 with K-sweep {10, 100, 1000}, all six methods, R = 30, plus one set_num_threads(4) sensitivity repeat, plus a default-tolerance-only sweep (or a full tolerance sweep if compute permits), plus the Adam sub-experiment at K = 100. Indicative wall-clock: low-to-mid double-digit CPU-hours.

Artifacts produced. A version manifest; a Source-verification appendix; per-cell HDF5 or JSON artifacts; a per-cell statistics table; an aggregate cross-cell table with Holm-adjusted p-values; an ablation table for the A-versus-C2 and B-versus-C2 comparisons; the Source-verification-rewritten implementation if the gate triggered a rewrite.

---

## (viii) Threats to validity

CPU-only environmental ceiling (primary). GPU is disabled in the runtime (gpu_enabled equals false). CUDA-leaning TorchOpt optimisations — kernel fusion, autograd-graph caching, compiled-graph reuse — are not measured on this host. The time axis reflects algorithmic-flop accounting and Python/CPU dispatch cost rather than end-to-end GPU performance. The stability axis is independent of GPU availability and remains the primary evidentiary axis on this host.

BLAS dependency. The exact BLAS implementation that ships with PyTorch (OpenBLAS or MKL) is a co-variate with timing, and to a lesser extent with numerical stability. Recorded in the manifest. Not swept within the design because sweeping BLAS would confound the method comparison.

Thread-scheduling dependence. Even with taskset -c 0-3, set_num_threads(1), OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, and MKL_NUM_THREADS=1, residual scheduler noise remains. Cells where the median-to-p95 ratio of dt_r exceeds 2 are reported with that caveat and are not aggregated into headline comparisons without the set_num_threads(4) sensitivity repeat passing.

Semantic drift of the TorchOpt API. The Source-verification gate (ix) is the only mitigation. If the verified surface does not match the documented surface, the design pivots; it does not relabel.

Absence of any published CPU-only TorchOpt benchmark. There is no published baseline of TorchOpt performance on CPU. The magnitude claims in H1, H2, H3, H4 cannot be anchored against prior literature for this host; the experiment generates fresh data without that anchor.

Fairness of the create_graph=True documented-form baseline. Held by binding D4 to the standard form with no allow_unused, no torch.compile, no manual activation checkpointing. This may not represent practitioner best-practices; the best-practices variant is recorded only in section (x) as a single-line future path on a GPU host.

Synthetic-data external validity. T1 and T2 use synthetic data so that the conditioning axis is controllable. The conclusions may not transfer unchanged to real datasets; this is a documented scope choice in (ii), recorded here as a threat only at the level of cross-data-set generalisation.

Single-task and scalar-scope decisions. The inner loop is single-task and the outer hyperparameter is scalar. Multi-task (MAML-style task averaging) inner loops and vector-valued outer hyperparameters are recorded as open questions in (x); they are out of scope and are not threats to the per-cell conclusions within scope.

Effect-size threshold calibration. The |Delta-tilde / IQR| at-least-0.5 threshold is reasonable for R = 30 but is not a literature standard for hypergradient comparisons. Paired Cohen's d and Cliff's delta are computed from the recorded per-cell data and recorded as sensitivity descriptors.

---

## (x) Limitations and open questions

Best-practices create_graph path. A single-line acknowledgement only: a create_graph=True plus torch.compile baseline on a GPU host is the practitioner-best-practices comparator. It is outside this design's scope and is recorded as the natural next step on a CUDA-equipped execution host only.

Multi-task inner loop. Whether the A-versus-B-versus-C2 separation of effects reproduces under task averaging (MAML-style) is open. The design's scope limit is single-task; an extension would add a multi-task cell at K = 5 inner steps on a single representative task distribution but only as an additional experiment, not as part of the headline ablation.

Vector-valued outer hyperparameters. Whether the implicit-diff reuse advantage persists or grows when the outer hyperparameter is vector-valued (multiple regularizer strengths or per-layer learning rates) is open. The current design restricts the outer hyperparameter to scalar in both tasks to keep the analytical reference for T1 and the central-difference reference for T2 tractable.

K-sweep extrapolation. The K-sweep {10, 100, 1000} spans the MAML-relevant inner-loop length range; extrapolation beyond K = 1000 is unverified by this design.

Source-drift rebuild cadence. The Source-verification gate runs once per execution. If TorchOpt modifies the implicit-diff API between the gate pass and the run, the design must be re-gated.

Finite-difference precision floor for T2. Central finite differences at h approximately 1e-5 in float64 have a known bias of order O(h squared). Cells whose rel_err_T2 value is comparable to or smaller than this floor are reported as "below FD precision floor" rather than as "no error" and are excluded from H2 claims for T2.

Best-practices create_graph acknowledgment. Restated for emphasis: the create_graph=True + torch.compile practitioner-best-practices baseline is recorded as a single-line future path on a GPU host in this Limitations section only.

T3 (CNN) re-entry condition. T3 is dropped from the design and re-enters only if, during execution or pre-execution review, the stability axis is demonstrated to be underdetermined by T1 and T2 alone. No such underdetermination has been identified in this draft.

Ablation-table collapse condition. The three-way A-versus-B-versus-C2 table is preserved as the primary ablation. It collapses to two independent pairwise comparisons (A versus C2 and B versus C2) only if the Source-verification gate finds that TorchOpt exposes only a single differentiable path that does not allow the implicit-diff reuse and the MetaOptimizer-state reuse effects to be separated.

create_graph with torch.compile on a GPU host. Recorded once more for completeness: this is out of scope on the CPU-only host and lives only as a future research direction in the Limitations section.

Stable comparator set. C1, C3, and C4 are reported as context and reference respectively, never as headline baselines. The headline baselines are C2 (the documented-standard-form unrolled create_graph=True comparator required by D4) plus the IMPL reference C4 for the stability axis.

Open question — solver internals. Whether the implicit-diff solver exposes kappa(A) and norm(A v minus g) directly, or whether these must be reconstructed post-hoc from the assembled A, is a source-verification item. The post-hoc reconstruction path is the fallback.

Open question — R chosen. R = 30 is the operational choice balancing power against compute budget. A higher R (for example 50 or 100) would tighten the effect-size threshold; this is recorded as a future-budget sensitivity rather than a binding constraint.

No execution in this environment. This is a design-only artifact. No experiment was run. No per-cell artifacts were produced. No plots are claimed. The Source-verification gate has not been passed in this environment because TorchOpt is not installed and the network is disabled.
